See title. Tried to invite a member via QR code; the app kept pushing them to set up a bridge or add lights before completing set up in order to join the home.

Great hardware; very frustrating software.

reviews.title: …no shortcut compatibility?
reviews.text: Absolutely insane that hue isn’t available in the shortcuts app. I regret buying a sync box, because now I need to activate/deactivate automations AND manually start the sync by opening the app and starting it.. when I should be able to create a shortcut to deactivate and activate things with the click of a button or (more importantly for me) my voice.. and then their faq just points you towards some abstract techy hoopla about creating a url to use within shortcuts.. how is that user friendly by any means? Between that and all the other terrible decisions signify has been making with hue, I regret ever investing in them. At least the lights work most of the time through HomeKit. But do not buy a sync box with the led strip for your tv unless you want it to become a headache to enjoy every time you want to.

reviews.title: Horrible App & Horrible Bulbs
reviews.text: The app is so annoying. Why the hell does a light bulb need an update!? I can’t use my lights without being bothered about an update. Not to mention that my lights bulbs like to disconnect themselves from the app whenever they want. And they are such a pain in the hooohaaah to get reconnected. 10/10 do not recommend. Waste of money.

reviews.title: Most unintuitive app ever
reviews.text: Simple instructions would be appreciated. I didn’t think this app could get worse, but it has. Now I no longer able to switch scenes and have it stay saved. All the fancy stuff doesn’t matter when it doesn’t stay saved. I realized I’m communicating into the void, but I’d sure like it to be simpler than it is. I thought this would be fun, it most definitely is not.

reviews.title: It does what it’s supposed to do, that’s it
reviews.text: The interface is a bit clunky and setting up anything is difficult. Light settings are not saved so every time they come on, they are at full brightness and original color, I have to readjust every time. Why do I have to set up zones and rooms? There should be an option to set up individual lights without having to set up a whole new zone.

reviews.title: Itch the Glitch!
reviews.text: Wow- this app BLOWS!  I’ve never used an app that is so chock full of glitches!  Simple things, like change room require me to chase the selection all over my screen. Come on, you can do better. Hire some beta testers and don’t release until it’s glitch free- pretty simple!

reviews.title: FIX THE ENTERTAINMENT AREAS LIGHT PLACEMENT!!!!
reviews.text: It’s ridiculous that the placement of all the lights around the TV is constricted to 10% of the phone screen. It can’t be zoomed for fine tuning. The screen real estate is big, use it properly.

reviews.title: Developers Screwed Up Sensors Again
reviews.text:
UPDATE:

It turns out Phillips has managed to completely screw up everything related to the sensors, not just the bug they introduced below. Lights continuously turn on even without the sensors detecting motion. Rather than following the time-based sensor rules, sensors ignore the settings in the app and turn lights on “dim” or 100% brightness regardless of time of day. One light won’t turn off. It dims to about 5%, but doesn’t shut off (and that one is not controlled by a sensor). The troubleshooting steps are useless. I have reset the dysfunctional sensors, deleted them, replaced the batteries, and completely reprogrammed the settings. Nothing works. Seriously, Philips, make your software engineers test EVERY app function before pushing out app updates. 


 How hard is it to test features before releasing an app update?

Hue’s software engineers screwed up the motion sensors yet again. The sunrise/sunset capability literally doesn’t work at all. It’s supposed to suppress automation actions between sunrise and sunset (like don’t turn on a light if motion is detected). They also screwed up automations. I have a sensor set to “do nothing” between 7:30 am and 5:00 pm when motion is detected, yet all freaking day, every day, the sensor turns the light on.  These are basic core features of the app. Test your work.

reviews.title: Decision Fatigue
reviews.text: More often than not, I want a dimmer switch more than I want my desk lamp to turn purple. If I leave the room and turn off my lights after setting a custom brightness (e.g. turning down a desk lamp because it’s bright outside) I have no way to easily return to this custom, temporary state. I want to save power, but I also don’t want to spend a minute fidgeting with my lights to get that perfect brightness again. When I return to the room, I can choose a custom preset (good feature), or individually turn on lights. One misclick on the binary slider for a light opens a detailed menu for colors that I rarely use. This menu has many buttons, and is distracting when I just want a simple, large dimmer switch to push most of the time. Also, it is not possible to remove some preset scenes from the menu. I want a clean, simple experience for my light switch. I don’t need my lights to have a green and purple button that I can’t hide. Yes, it’s awesome your lights do that. I’ll use it on Halloween. No, I don’t want that button prominent in the menu the other 364 days of the year. The app has great potential, but is frustrating for one of my common use cases. I still love the lights, but I find the current app interface detrimental to the experience.

reviews.title: Absolute DISAPPOINTMENT, DISGRACE and underperformance
reviews.text: Absolute DISAPPOINTMENT, DISGRACE and underperformance for outside use of cameras. Cameras does not record everything happening. You are limited to min 10sec spread between recorded events and max 60 sec one recording . How it’s choosing where to start and stop record clip is absolute not logic - if for ex. you get people hanging around in front of camera for long time the chances are you would not get recorded actual act of vandalism like throw of stone. Because it’s does not record one clip straight after another but god knows how it’s decide when to start and stop recorded clip. I believe Philips does it on purpose to save servers space occupied with recorded videos. Besides if you get multiple events recorded overnight quite often not all of them get shown in app listing , you have to watch one after another to make sure none is missing. Besides motion sensors usually take ages to load events or often does not load at all. If you look for serious security looks elsewhere as this one is serious disappoint especially for this price. I bought Philips (and avoided Chinese) for privacy reason but for this price I have not expected this level of „extrements”. Avoid for time being until they will address all this and clearly make improvement statements on their nice looking website. Last think is problem with spiders which makes webs around lens and webs shaking makes it recording whole night (talking outside cameras overnight with infrared LED flashing and making webs visible )

reviews.title: Expensive/Time consuming
reviews.text: I bought a $100 Go lamp to use as a morning alarm clock. I tried to schedule a daily sunrise. It isn’t allowed. I have to go in and manually set it every night. I also have to set a sun set to turn it off after a while or it will never turn off unless I go into the app and manually turn it off. So, every night I have to go and turn the two schedules on if I want to use them. If I forget, then it doesn’t do anything. If I want full access to the scheduling features, I must go out and purchase a $70 Bridge, for just one lamp. So, that is about $170 to get the one Go lamp to work as it should. I bought a set of four WiFi smart plugs for $30 and have full functionality and can set multiple separate schedules for each of the devices without issues. They just work once set. How is it that a $30 set of smart plugs are fully featured and can have multiple schedules, while a $100 smart lamp is dumb and requires extra daily steps or an extra purchase to work? Make that make sense. Very disappointed. Do better Hue.

reviews.title: Garbage if you have Unifi
reviews.text:
If you have Unifi network gear and want to get this working then best of luck especially if you have separate IOT Vlans.  Have been trying to get working with Apple HomeKit for ages now only to get no response on all devices. I even bought  the new Philips pro bridge still no different. 

For quite a period of time I couldn’t get even the hue app to control the lights but at least have that working. I have found the app to handy often, and Alexa response  is very slow. 

The “it just works” no longer applies here and there are now much better and cheaper options out there now for which I will be moving away from hue altogether as I’ve had enough. I have no trouble with any other IOT devices on my network only Philips hue and it seems their matter implementation may be the issue, as up to that point everything worked flawlessly.

reviews.title: Nightmare with Hue Bridge Pro with HomeKit
reviews.text: I have been a loyal Philips Hue user for over a decade.  The selling point of “it just works, and works well” is no longer.  I was having intermittent issues with my old v2 bridge so I decided to upgrade to the pro bridge.  What a mistake that was!!!  Avoid this at all costs if you’re a HomeKit user.  The issues with HomeKit have been a nightmare.  What started out as intermittent connectivity issues a few times a month spiraled into becoming a daily occurrence.  I saw an update for Apple TV OS and decided to update hoping it would fix my issues.  Welp…that was a mistake!!  My hue bridge pro no longer even connects to HomeKit at all!!! I’d love to go back to the daily disconnects at this point but I can’t even do that now.  Through investigation I’ve learned that my hue bridge pro is stuck on an older firmware version that is incompatible with the new TVos.  They’ve been working on this fix for months now, and apparently they have it, but they slowly roll out the updates.  Since the HUE app doesn’t let you manually pull down updates, I am now stuck in this nightmare.  Why oh why did you not push out the update earlier, or send out warnings to people to not update their Apple devices to the newest OS until you “get around” to rolling out the updates to us.  This might be the last straw for me.  I’ve spent thousands of dollars on hue products over the years, and you may have finally lost me.  At the very least you need to allow people to manually request firmware updates like A
